WITH o AS (SELECT subtotal, CASE WHEN subtotal < 500 THEN 'under $5' WHEN subtotal < 1000 THEN '$5 to $10' WHEN subtotal < 2000 THEN '$10 to $20' ELSE '$20 or more' END band FROM orders WHERE ordered_at >= '2025-01-01' AND ordered_at < '2026-01-01')
SELECT band, COUNT(*) n, SUM(subtotal)/100.0 sales, SUM(subtotal)*1.0/SUM(SUM(subtotal)) OVER () share, (SELECT MAX(ordered_at) FROM orders) mx, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE subtotal IS NULL) nulls FROM o GROUP BY band ORDER BY MIN(subtotal)

args.sql:
WITH o AS (SELECT subtotal, CASE WHEN subtotal < 500 THEN 'under $5' WHEN subtotal < 1000 THEN '$5 to $10' WHEN subtotal < 2000 THEN '$10 to $20' ELSE '$20 or more' END band FROM orders WHERE ordered_at >= '2025-01-01' AND ordered_at < '2026-01-01')
SELECT band, COUNT(*) n, SUM(subtotal)/100.0 sales, SUM(subtotal)*1.0/SUM(SUM(subtotal)) OVER () AS shr, (SELECT MAX(ordered_at) FROM orders) mx, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE subtotal IS NULL) AS nnull FROM o GROUP BY band ORDER BY MIN(subtotal)

args.message:
I grouped all 408,306 orders from calendar 2025 by their pre-tax value (subtotal in cents ÷ 100). Each band includes its lower limit and excludes its upper one, so a $5.00 order counts in "$5 to $10". Sales are pre-tax dollars, and each share is the band's sales divided by total 2025 sales of $4,296,716. No orders were missing a value.

- **Under $5:** 60,191 orders, $229,504 in sales, share 0.0534
- **$5 to $10:** 232,467 orders, $1,401,521 in sales, share 0.3262
- **$10 to $20:** 71,778 orders, $1,118,561 in sales, share 0.2603
- **$20 or more:** 43,870 orders, $1,547,130 in sales, share 0.3601

Orders of $20 or more are only about 11% of orders but bring in the largest share of sales, about 36%. The $5 to $10 band has the most orders, at 57%.
